summary: This excerpt from a fiction novel (Book 3, part 115) follows a first-person narrator who parts from Steve, who drives off in his Jeep, as the narrator resolves to search for Sarah alone, keeping Steve out of danger. The narrator recalls a frightening past descent into the Red Fort's harem quarters in Agra and tries to persuade Alan, who is reluctant, to take them to a look at a place. Alan hesitates and mentions a concern about the rulers of the paradise-like location, then agrees to go after the weather clears. The narrator reasons that Sarah's last known location was the Peten, where Ramos likely took her, and identifies Baalum as the destination. The passage ends with the narrator in a budget hotel room planning to call St. Vincent's to check on Lou and to tell someone what is happening.
one_line: A narrator parts from Steve, plans a dangerous search for Sarah in the Peten, and arranges to check on Lou from a budget hotel room.
key_facts: The narrator tells Steve, "I don't have you. Don't worry. I'll be okay."
Steve says, "It's only for a couple of days," and "We'll both be okay if we just stick together."
The narrator watches Steve's Jeep blend into the smoggy haze of the avenue.
The narrator is determined to find Sarah before something else truly horrible happens to her.
The narrator recalls going down into the four-hundred-year-old subterranean harem quarters of the Red Fort in Agra, pitch black and knee-deep in guano.
Alan says he will plead guilty to a deep-seated disquiet about the people who rule the placid paradise.
Alan agrees to take the narrator up for a quick look after the weather clears.
The narrator notes that Alan is already thinking about his next loan.
The narrator says the Peten is where Sarah ended up the first time and where Ramos has likely taken her now.
The word Baalum is mentioned as the destination the narrator is sure of.
The narrator is in a hotel room with off-brand carpet, two double beds, and a TV bolted to the wall above the dresser.
The narrator plans to call St. Vincent's to check on Lou.
The narrator asks the desk for the local AT&T contact number before placing the call.
